learning.title: Deploy Railway from GitHub Actions when the Railway GitHub App is absent
learning.trigger: A task wants Railway autodeploy from GitHub main after CI, but the Railway GitHub App is not installed on the organization.
learning.rule: Native GitHub autodeploy was not available: the Railway GitHub App was not installed on the GitHub organization (installing it needs an organization admin), and Wait for CI skips any deploy whose checks run longer than 2 hours while main CI runs reached 6 hours 22 minutes.

Use a workflow_run workflow on Bakery CI success for main that runs railway up --detach --json per service with a single-environment project token, captures that upload's deployment id, and polls only that id to SUCCESS. Never report success from the upload alone: pre-deploy and the health check run after it returns.

The job keeps contents: read only, takes RAILWAY_TOKEN from one secret, aborts the rollout when the API deployment fails, and skips only when /health/ready reports the SHA or a descendant and every service has a newest SUCCESS deployment for it (newest by createdAt; an undated record counts as unproven) and the dispatcher still passes the liveness log read. The api deploys first, so the reported version alone proves nothing about dispatcher or web: a rerun after a partial failure must redeploy the laggards.

The workflow checks out the candidate SHA and runs the candidate's own scripts/deploy/railway-deploy.ts. When main CI is queued for hours, a green CI run for a commit older than the workflow can finish after the workflow lands; that commit has no script, so the job failed with "Module not found". The workflow now checks for the script right after checkout and skips the rest with a notice. A workflow_run failure on an old SHA is that case, not a token fault: read the failed step before blaming the secret.

Bound the per-deployment poll by how long one status lasts, never by the deployment's total duration. Railway's build queue is sometimes several times slower than usual (run 40735281134, 2026-10-28: api and dispatcher took 45 minutes against a normal 7), and a total-duration bound then fails a deployment that is merely slow. That run reported web TIMEOUT after 25 min (last status DEPLOYING) at 18:33, while Railway removed the previous web deployment at 18:44:26 — it promoted the deployment the script had just abandoned, so QA stayed on the older SHA for about six hours while CI reported red. A deployment that genuinely fails its health check is marked FAILED or CRASHED, which the status check already catches, so the time bound only has to catch one that stops reporting progress at all.

Keep the job's timeout-minutes above the script's own rollout cap. A per-service bound multiplied by the service count silently exceeded it before (25 min x 4 services = 100 min against timeout-minutes: 90), and a job killed by its own timeout reports no failure at all. One shared rollout budget plus a rail asserting the two numbers stay ordered is what keeps them from drifting apart.

The guard recognises a deployment as current only by its upload message: railway up -m "main SHA" (deploymentMessage in scripts/deploy/railway-deploy.ts), read back as meta.cliMessage. A hand upload counts as current only with exactly that text. Use "main SHA" for a commit on main; any other text, such as "candidate SHA" for a build that is not on main, counts as lagging and the next workflow run supersedes it.

verification.requirement: Record the deployment id, its final status from railway deployment list, and the /health/ready version equal to the SHA.

Recorded 2026-10-25 on CLI 5.71.0: railway up --detach --json prints {deploymentId, logsUrl}; railway deployment list --json items are {createdAt, id, meta, status} and the -m text is meta.cliMessage; statuses seen are INITIALIZING, BUILDING, DEPLOYING, SUCCESS, FAILED, REMOVING, REMOVED. Re-capture if the CLI major changes.

learning.boundary: It is not known whether a Railway redeploy triggered by a variable or config change keeps meta.cliMessage. If it does not, the guard fails closed: a same-SHA rerun re-uploads the service, and a late run for an older SHA ends red with DEPLOYED_SERVICES_STALE. The workflow cannot be dispatched before it exists on main. Native GitHub source stays an optional later switch that needs an organization admin to install the App.
